props.title: Risk triage (risicoclassificatie)
props.subtitle: Drag a system into the tier it belongs to. The first column is everything nobody has decided about yet.

props.title: Unclassified is not a neutral state
props.text: A system nobody has classified is a system nobody has checked against Article 5 or Annex III. It sits in the red column until someone decides — which is the whole point of the column being there.

props.emptyText: No tiers configured — add them on Setup.

props.title: Picking the use case sets the tier
props.text: Each use case carries the tier it triggers, so choosing the row that matches this system classifies it and records which Annex III point (or Article 50 duty) the classification rests on. Change the rule itself on Setup.

props.emptyText: No use cases configured — add them on Setup.

props.name: description
props.label: What went wrong, and to whom

props.title: The reporting deadline is set for you
props.text: Pick a serious severity and the register computes the Article 73 deadline from the date you became aware: 15 days normally, 10 where a person died, 2 for a widespread infringement or a serious disruption of critical infrastructure.

props.emptyText: This system has never been assessed.

screens.name: Incidents
screens.description: What went wrong, and what still has to be reported.

props.title: Incidents (ernstige incidenten)
props.subtitle: Log incidents on the system itself. This screen is where you see which ones are still owed to a supervisory authority.

props.title: Article 73 — reporting a serious incident
props.text: The deadline runs from the day you became **aware**, not the day it happened: 15 days as a rule, 10 days where a person died, 2 days for a widespread infringement or a serious and irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure. Record the notification here so the register shows it was made.

props.emptyText: No incidents recorded. Log one from the system it happened on.
Open an incident from the list.

props.label: Record the notification as sent today

screens.name: Setup
screens.description: Risk tiers and Annex III use cases.

props.title: Setup
props.subtitle: The tiers and the use cases are data, not code. Add a tier and the triage board grows a column; change a use case's tier and the next system classified against it follows the new rule.

props.title: Two things to know
props.text: A tier added here appears on the triage board immediately, but the tier dropdown in the register's filter bar is a fixed list — it only grows when an editor adds it. And changing a use case's tier does not reclassify the systems already pointing at it: classification is a decision with a date on it, so it is re-made on the system, never rewritten underneath you.

props.label: What it obliges us to do

steps.message: Registered — it is unclassified until someone triages it.
Pick the automation that sends the reminder under Automations — this button is wired to nothing until you do.
Reclassified. Record why on the system, under Assessments.
Classified from the use case. Record the reasoning under Assessments.
Incident logged. If it is serious, the reporting deadline is on the Incidents screen.
Assessment recorded, and the system's review dates moved with it.
Notification recorded. An incident already reported keeps the date it was reported on — add the authority's reference in the grid.
Tier added — the triage board has a column for it now.
